instruction: `click.ParamType` takes its context arguments in the opposite order from the rest of its API: `shell_complete(ctx, param, incomplete)` is context-first, but `convert(value, param, ctx)`, `fail(message, param=None, ctx=None)`, `get_metavar(param, ctx)` and `get_missing_message(param, ctx)` are not, which keeps producing swapped arguments in custom types. Make all of them context-first (src/click/types.py): rename `convert` to `convert_value(self, ctx, param, value)` and `fail` to `reject(self, ctx, param, message)` (all three arguments required, no defaults; it still raises `BadParameter(message, ctx=ctx, param=param)`), and reorder `get_metavar(self, ctx, param)` and `get_missing_message(self, ctx, param)` keeping their names. Apply this to the base `ParamType` and every subclass that defines these methods -- the built-in types in src/click/types.py and every custom `ParamType` in the tests and examples -- and update every call: `self.convert(...)`/`super().convert(...)`/`SomeType().convert(...)` become `convert_value` calls and `self.fail(...)` inside a type becomes `self.reject(...)`, each with the arguments it passed before moved into the new order (pass `None` where a `fail` call relied on the old `None` defaults); positional calls of `get_metavar`/`get_missing_message` must be reordered too (this includes a bound `convert` method kept in a variable, and code a test runs in a subprocess). Do not keep the old names as aliases or wrappers. Do not change `ParamType.__call__(value, param=None, ctx=None)` (it keeps its signature and calls `convert_value`), `Context.fail(message)`, `shell_complete`, or `Parameter.type_cast_value(ctx, value)`. Behavior must not change.
gold_tool: build_deep.py recipe: masked-text call finder (deep_edit) locates every convert/fail definition and call on a ParamType (receiver self/super()/a type instance; Context.fail and the nested convert() closures in core.py excluded); arguments re-emitted in the new order from their positional/keyword spans; click's suite in docker confirms
change: two renames + argument reorder (convert -> convert_value, fail -> reject) and two reorders (get_metavar, get_missing_message) across every ParamType and every call
notes: Shapes: the identifier `convert` (nested `def convert(value)` closures in core.py are identical in base and gold, so they cancel), ParamType fail calls/defs, and the old-order get_metavar/get_missing_message definitions. Swapped arguments are caught by click's error-message tests (BadParameter renders the param name) and by test_types' direct convert calls.

problem_statement: `click.ParamType` takes its context arguments in the opposite order from the rest of its API: `shell_complete(ctx, param, incomplete)` is context-first, but `convert(value, param, ctx)`, `fail(message, param=None, ctx=None)`, `get_metavar(param, ctx)` and `get_missing_message(param, ctx)` are not, which keeps producing swapped arguments in custom types. Make all of them context-first (src/click/types.py): rename `convert` to `convert_value(self, ctx, param, value)` and `fail` to `reject(self, ctx, param, message)` (all three arguments required, no defaults; it still raises `BadParameter(message, ctx=ctx, param=param)`), and reorder `get_metavar(self, ctx, param)` and `get_missing_message(self, ctx, param)` keeping their names. Apply this to the base `ParamType` and every subclass that defines these methods -- the built-in types in src/click/types.py and every custom `ParamType` in the tests and examples -- and update every call: `self.convert(...)`/`super().convert(...)`/`SomeType().convert(...)` become `convert_value` calls and `self.fail(...)` inside a type becomes `self.reject(...)`, each with the arguments it passed before moved into the new order (pass `None` where a `fail` call relied on the old `None` defaults); positional calls of `get_metavar`/`get_missing_message` must be reordered too (this includes a bound `convert` method kept in a variable, and code a test runs in a subprocess). Do not keep the old names as aliases or wrappers. Do not change `ParamType.__call__(value, param=None, ctx=None)` (it keeps its signature and calls `convert_value`), `Context.fail(message)`, `shell_complete`, or `Parameter.type_cast_value(ctx, value)`. Behavior must not change.
